bull.b: Rapid revenue expansion broadens GameSquare’s commercial base and indicates that acquired platforms and existing agency and intellectual-property activities are gaining scale. If sustained, this growth can improve operating leverage and strengthen the company’s position in gaming media and marketing.

The substantial gross-margin improvement and move to positive adjusted EBITDA provide evidence of better monetization and integration across the portfolio. Continued margin expansion would give revenue growth greater earnings quality and could create a clearer path toward sustainable operating profitability.

TubeBuddy’s high-margin SaaS economics, strong agency renewals, and substantial booked revenue improve visibility beyond one-off campaign wins. These characteristics can support more predictable revenue, protect gross margins, and provide a stronger foundation for scaling the broader gaming ecosystem.

bear.b: Despite top-line growth, GameSquare remains deeply unprofitable and continues consuming cash. Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits limit internally funded investment, increase dependence on external capital, and leave execution improvements unproven until revenue growth converts into durable earnings.

The sharp increase in debt relative to equity weakens the company’s financial cushion while losses remain substantial. Higher leverage can constrain capital allocation and make the business less resilient if integration takes longer, profitability disappoints, or additional funding becomes necessary.

The proposed FanEngine transaction could expand digital fan engagement, but its stock consideration would materially dilute existing holders and add contingent obligations. Combining this dilution with GameSquare’s losses may increase the financing burden before the acquired assets demonstrate sufficient earnings contribution.
